drafter_arguments.datedness_tie: A has one condition predicate ('era-specific dated finish') governing three location disjuncts (casing, jambs, baseboards), so every disjunct is tied to datedness by construction: nothing bills unless the FINISH reads dated for its era, and the location list only says where the finish must be seen. Visible tells per disjunct, from the photos I opened: on casing, a heavy dark-stained or taupe-painted casing on a cased opening whose colour and profile belong to an earlier scheme (redfin_80990371/photo_022, photo_028); on jambs, aged painted panel doors and their jambs with chipped, uneven paint (redfin_80990371/photo_029); on baseboards, tall or mismatched painted baseboards carrying the same dated colour scheme (redfin_80990371/photo_028). The word 'dated' is doing the work in every branch, which is exactly ruling 4's wording ('an identifiable era-specific finish or visible deterioration qualifies', HANDOFF_SESSION_2.md:74-93). The weakness is not the tie but the tell's discriminating power: 'era-specific' is a property of the MILLWORK PROFILE as much as of the finish, and period millwork has an era-specific profile even when its finish is current (redfin_11185681/photo_006, photo_044).
drafter_arguments.kill_condition: A is the riskier of the two on rc_73d15ca14405 and I will not pretend otherwise. Terra is shown 'interior trim era-specific dated finish on casing, jambs, or baseboards' (terra_review.py:76-90) inside a payload that also carries the frozen 2b observations 'The chair rail and wainscot-style division are dated.' and 'The trim is basic and dated.'. Photos 006 and 044 show a genuine period trim package - crown, chair rail, panel moulding, deep window casings, a radiator cover - whose profile is unmistakably era-specific, uniformly repainted in a clean current white. Three signals in the payload say 'dated' and only the reader's willingness to separate profile from finish says otherwise, and CCF-3 records that on the frozen record Terra echoed bare style-word claims as supported 15 of 18 times, engaged a qualifier in only 10 of 33 rationales and rejected on one in 2. The production prompt (terra_review.py:33-51) has no literal-reading or negation rule to lean on. I therefore expect A to be the candidate most likely to flip the correct rejection into a manufactured hallucination, and the live check on rc_73d15ca14405 is the only thing that can settle it. Steven's recorded concern - 'era-specific' sits one word from 'period millwork' - is, on the pixels, correct.
drafter_arguments.would_bill_intact_dark_trim: Probably not on the wording, but the wording is not what decides it. A requires the finish to read DATED for its era; well-kept, intentionally dark-stained trim in good condition is a current design choice and fails that test on a literal reading. But the reading has to be literal, and CCF-3 says production Terra frequently is not: a payload whose 2b observation says 'dark wood trim' with no datedness word would still put a dark-finish description in front of a claim containing the word 'dated'. There is no adjudicated control in the CAP-008 evidence to test this: the only reviewed dark-trim card in the family is rc_b642fe69b86a (redfin_80990371/photo_022), which was adjudicated supports_claim as genuinely dated, so no intact, non-dated dark-stained trim control exists to catch the over-reach in either direction.
drafter_arguments.would_bill_clean_white_period_trim: My prediction is YES, supported - the failure mode. On photos 006 and 044 the profile is era-specific, the payload's own observations assert datedness twice, and A's state contains no positive predicate that the white multi-coat finish demonstrably violates. The only thing standing between A and a 'supported' verdict is Terra choosing to read 'finish' as distinct from 'profile'. Nothing in the production prompt asks it to. This is the single reason I flag A as the compliant-but-fragile candidate, and the reason the live check on rc_73d15ca14405 is a blocking gate rather than a formality.

drafter_arguments.datedness_tie: B FAILS the Q-4 tie on its first disjunct, and I record that as a defect rather than arguing around it. Parsed as '[dark-stained wood] or [dated paint color]', only the second disjunct carries a datedness word; the first makes a colour fact sufficient. The visible tell for disjunct 1 is simply 'the trim is dark-stained wood' - true of the heavy dark casings at redfin_80990371/photo_022 (which IS dated) and equally true of a deliberately dark-stained modern trim package in perfect condition, which is not. That is precisely Steven's recorded concern: it replaces 'plain means billable' with 'dark means billable'. The visible tell for disjunct 2 is a trim colour belonging to an earlier scheme - the wide taupe-painted window casings and tall baseboards at redfin_80990371/photo_028 and the aged taupe doors and jambs at photo_029 - and that disjunct is properly tied. The minimal repair is to let 'dated' govern both branches (for example 'dated dark-stained or painted finish on casing and baseboards'), which I am NOT licensed to author here: the brief permits a third candidate only if BOTH A and B fail the tie, and A does not fail it.
drafter_arguments.kill_condition: B is the safer of the two on rc_73d15ca14405. Photos 006 and 044 show a uniform, clean, multi-coat WHITE finish over the period millwork: 'dark-stained wood' is concretely and visibly false, and 'dated paint color' is false of a current neutral white unless Terra treats the observation's word 'dated' as the answer to a colour question. CCF-3's census cuts the other way here - concrete positive predicates were rejected 13 of 17 times when absent - so B has the profile of a claim Terra rejects on these photos. The residual risk is that the payload's observations ('The chair rail and wainscot-style division are dated.', 'The trim is basic and dated.') supply the word 'dated' and Terra matches word to word rather than colour to pixels; that is not settleable offline either, which is why B needs the same live check. B's real danger is the opposite error: over-acceptance on dark objects, including dark objects that are not trim (redfin_25809814/photo_020 carries an espresso vanity and a dark-stained mirror frame in the same frame as the plain white baseboard the claim is supposed to reject), and CCF-3 records Terra affirming 'entry or window opening' while its rationale described a gable opening. The live-check card set does not test that failure mode at all.
drafter_arguments.would_bill_intact_dark_trim: Yes - by construction, and that is the defect. 'dark-stained wood' is satisfied by any dark-stained trim regardless of condition, era or whether a buyer would touch it, so intact, deliberately dark-stained trim in good condition bills under B as Terra reads it. The evidence cannot bound the cost: I searched the CAP-008 family and the bundle extracts for an adjudicated intact, non-dated dark-stained trim control and there is none - the only dark-trim card is the recovery rc_b642fe69b86a, adjudicated dated. So the over-reach is real, untested, and invisible to the three live-check cards, which is the strongest argument against adopting B as drafted.
drafter_arguments.would_bill_clean_white_period_trim: My prediction is NO, unsupported - B's intended strength. Neither disjunct describes what photos 006 and 044 show: the finish is white, uniform and clean, and the millwork's era-specific PROFILE is not something B asks about at all, because B asks only about colour and stain. The frozen observations still assert datedness twice, so a word-matching verdict remains possible and the live check still decides; but B removes the collision Steven named on A ('era-specific' next to 'period millwork') instead of relying on Terra to resolve it.

cap007.cutover_notes: CCF-8 applies in full and is not proposal-specific. (1) No runtime alias table exists. requires_re_resolution and deprecated are manifest-only; the single runtime consumer is the publication gate, which rejects any row resolving to a deprecated split parent and names its successors in the error (publication_gate.py:141-162). (2) Stale ids fail hard: server per-image checkpoints are not keyed on the catalog, so a run resumed across the regeneration carries dated_window_treatment_valance and raises StaleCatalogItemId (analyzer_server.py:277-329). Drain or discard in-flight runs at cutover; do not resume across it. (3) backfill_kind_v2 is not a migration path here: it returns skip_current for any artifact already at the target ontology and catalog version (backfill_kind_v2.py:266-275) and otherwise re-resolves by support_any hits only, which cannot decide between the two successors for a bullet that names neither a fabric object nor a blind. (4) Both successors carry a new atomic_claim, so the projection fingerprint hashed into every Terra request changes and no stored Terra checkpoint survives; Sessions 5 and 6 must replay rather than reuse, and the offline-recompute hazard applies (a v4/v5 recompute without replaying stored verifications zeroes the affected conditions). (5) 'Detectable but unbilled' is a real runtime state, not a bookkeeping fiction: a Terra-supported condition on a route_override no_action item stays in observed_conditions and the FE envelope, is counted in dispositions_no_action and carries zero dollars (catalog_projection.py:46-72 resolve_terminal_route returns ('no_action','route_override_no_action') ahead of the no-economics check). The regression-register vocabulary cannot express it, which is why three ledger rows put the route outcome in note. (6) The split is not blocked by CCF-7: dated_window_treatment_valance is not among the ten repair_support_when_driven marker items, and the dry run confirms repair_support_marker_routes is empty for both successors. (7) The v1 catalog is untouched; this is a v2/3.2 decisions-file change regenerated through migrate_catalog_kind_v2, so nothing ships until the publication gate and the FE adapter see the new ids.
cap007.evidence_grounding: The blinds successor is a POLICY APPLICATION, not an evidence-backed defect repair - the same footing as CAP-008 under ruling 3. Ruling 5 (HANDOFF_SESSION_2.md:89-90) says blinds stay detectable but must be a no_action condition, and Q-1 extends it to blinds in any condition. route_override is authorable only on a split successor (INHERITED_FIELDS, migrate_catalog_kind_v2.py:68-80), and narrowing the parent in place would suppress valances and curtains, so a split is the only native shape that satisfies both halves of the ruling. landscaping_enhancement_opportunity is the precedent for a modernization-kind, route_override no_action split successor (it is a cross-kind split with basis discretionary_improvement; the presentation_only basis is separately precedented by staging_or_decluttering_opportunity and mismatched_or_inconsistent_furniture_staging); this would be the first same-kind split in the decisions file, which nothing in the generator or validator forbids because the split is by subject, not by state, and every existing no_action item in the catalog is modernization with basis presentation_only or discretionary_improvement (5 of 5 in the census), which is why the blinds claim is presentation_only rather than the dated_style the Session 2 draft used.
